title: MRI in colon carcinoma: diagnostic value in assessing pathologic regression with therapy
summary: For local staging in colon carcinoma, MRI has been used and researched only very cautiously so far. However, technical advances in equipment and sequencing technology have significantly reduced MRI examination time in recent years, and the value of MRI for the diagnosis of colon carcinoma is increasingly being redefined. Evaluation of improved measurement conditions in colorectal carcinoma is the aim of this study.

interventions.name: Due to the prospective design of the study, there are no additional risks for the patients. After inclusion of the patient in the study, imaging is routinely performed under therapy and follow-up is followed for up to 6 months. Additional examinations will not take place.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
● Diagnosis of colorectal carcinoma. 
● Request for routine clinical MRI of the liver for staging.
● Treatment plan with future potential resection of the primary (to determine pTRG) and distant metastases, if applicable.
Exclusion criteria:
● Contraindication to administration of buscopan to decrease intestinal motility.
● Non-diagnostic MRI examination of the colon.
